blocks.heading: Symptoms
blocks.text: The payment gateway returns HTTP 502 errors after the upstream connection pool is exhausted. Customer requests fail intermittently while health checks remain green.

blocks.heading: Root cause
blocks.text: A stale keep-alive policy leaves half-open upstream connections in the pool. The gateway reuses dead sockets until the connection acquisition timeout is reached.

blocks.heading: Repair
blocks.text: Drain the stale connection pool, reduce keep-alive duration, and restart only the affected gateway instances. Confirm recovery with successful payment authorization probes.

blocks.heading: Observability
blocks.text: The incident is observed by the upstream_connection_errors_total counter, connection_pool_pending gauge, and the payment_authorization_success_ratio dashboard.

blocks.heading: Atomic write
blocks.text: The business transaction stores both the domain change and the outbox event in the same PostgreSQL transaction.

blocks.heading: Publishing
blocks.text: A background publisher claims pending outbox rows and publishes them to the message broker using an idempotency key.

blocks.heading: Dead letter
blocks.text: After the retry limit is exhausted, the event moves to DEAD_LETTER and requires reconciliation before it can be replayed.

blocks.heading: Monitoring
blocks.text: Outbox delivery is observed by pending row age, publish retry count, dead-letter count, and broker acknowledgement latency.

blocks.heading: Compare
blocks.text: Reconciliation compares authoritative PostgreSQL state with external broker and vector index state.

blocks.heading: Repair
blocks.text: Missing external records are recreated from PostgreSQL, while orphan external records are quarantined before deletion.

blocks.heading: Replay
blocks.text: A dead-letter outbox event is replayed only after the underlying business state and idempotency key are verified.

blocks.heading: Proof
blocks.text: A repair is complete when counts match, checksums agree, no orphan records remain, and a read-after-write probe succeeds.

blocks.heading: Expiry
blocks.text: Expired records may be deleted after the configured retention window only when no active legal hold applies.

blocks.heading: Legal hold
blocks.text: An active legal hold prevents physical deletion even when the normal retention deadline has passed.

blocks.heading: Cleanup
blocks.text: The cleanup job marks eligible records, deletes external copies in bounded batches, and then removes PostgreSQL metadata according to policy.

blocks.heading: Audit
blocks.text: Every retention deletion records the policy version, decision time, actor, affected object, and legal-hold evaluation result.

blocks.heading: Mandatory filter
blocks.text: Every retrieval query must filter by access zone, caller access level, lifecycle status, expiry, and deletion state before ranking.

blocks.heading: Final recheck
blocks.text: Selected contexts are revalidated against PostgreSQL visibility rules immediately before the response is returned.

blocks.heading: Fail closed
blocks.text: Unknown access zones, invalid access levels, and stale visibility records are rejected without returning partial protected content.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.text: The gateway product provides a unified API for checkout, invoicing, refunds, and merchant analytics.

blocks.heading: Swimming pool promotion
blocks.text: The summer membership includes access to a heated swimming pool, lockers, towels, and weekend family sessions.

blocks.heading: Device repair
blocks.text: The service center repairs payment terminals, replaces cracked displays, and updates device firmware.

blocks.heading: Fraud response
blocks.text: Restricted fraud rules contain confidential thresholds and investigation procedures that must never be returned to public callers.

blocks.heading: Signals
blocks.text: The playbook correlates device reputation, velocity anomalies, beneficiary risk, and account takeover indicators.

blocks.heading: Seed pressure
blocks.text: When many nearly identical direct hits dominate the top ranks, a useful lower-ranked seed can be excluded from graph expansion.

blocks.heading: Seed diversity
blocks.text: A production seed selector should preserve high score while diversifying by logical block and document identity.

blocks.heading: Edge budget
blocks.text: Graph edge selection should distribute a bounded candidate budget across seeds instead of allowing the first seed to consume the global limit.
